item.title: Browser Detection with PHP
item.description:
Did you know that PHP includes a built-in function to detect which browser a visitor is using?

You can try this simple snippet:

<?php
$get_visitor_browser = get_browser(null, true);
print_r($get_visitor_browser);
?>

The get_browser() function returns an associative array (or object) containing detailed information about the user’s browser, such as:

[browser_name_regex] => ^mozilla/5.0 (windows; .*; windows nt 5.1.*) gecko/.* firefox/1.5.*$
[browser_name_pattern] => Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; *; Windows NT 5.1*) Gecko/* Firefox/1.5*
[parent] => Firefox 1.5
[platform] => WinXP
[browser] => Firefox
[version] => 1.5
[majorver] => 1
[minorver] => 5
[css] => 2
[frames] => 1
[iframes] => 1
[tables] => 1
[cookies] => 1
[javascript] => 1
[javaapplets] => 1

To make this function work correctly, you’ll need an updated browscap.ini file and must configure PHP to use it.
